content: Kinectin is a protein encoded by the KTN1 gene in humans. Various cellular organelles and vesicles are transported along microtubules within the cytoplasm. This transport process is essential for several cellular functions, including the recycling of membranes in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the assembly of the Golgi apparatus at the microtubule organizing center, and the alignment of lysosomes along microtubules. The movement of organelles along microtubules requires specific microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs). One such protein is kinesin, a molecular motor that functions as an ATPase. Kinesin facilitates the unidirectional movement of vesicles toward the plus end of the microtubule. Another important MAP involved in this process is kinectin, a large integral membrane protein located in the ER. Research has demonstrated that antibodies targeting kinectin can inhibit its ability to bind to kinesin, thereby interfering with its function. The KTN1 gene product, kinectin, has been shown to interact with several other proteins, including EEF1D (eukaryotic elongation factor 1 delta), RhoG, and RHOA. These interactions suggest that kinectin plays a role in various cellular processes beyond its involvement in microtubule-based transport.
